strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the release-risk assessment for Runtime module boundaries so autonomous headless execution no longer depends on an unbounded monolith-decomposition blocker.
Keeps permission, admission, replay, MCP approval, and completion authority in Rust Runtime while guarding extracted module ownership against drift.
Moves task.list transport bounding into the task_progress boundary and guards controlled tool execution and MCP approval boundaries as separate Runtime modules.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by converting the open module-decomposition concern into a guarded source-metric assessment plus one behavior-preserving task.list extraction.
answers.new_capability: Runtime module ownership is now assessed by docs/architecture/runtime-module-decomposition-assessment.json and enforced by guard:runtime-module-decomposition, including source metrics, boundary tokens, lib.rs production/test ceilings, and task.list transport-bound ownership.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M64.15 left runtime-module-decomposition open because prior extracted modules existed but no finite closure assessment or drift guard proved the remaining lib.rs shape was acceptable before release.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: The release loop would keep a subjective module-decomposition blocker open, and future changes could move task.list/progress or other Runtime authority back into lib.rs without a failing check.
answers.non_duplicative: This closes the module-decomposition reevaluation blocker; it is not another protocol/event, durable schema, MCP approval/recovery, CI workflow hardening, or platform/deadline/durability phase.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-6 adds no JSON-RPC methods and preserves existing task.list, progress, tool, MCP, Mode Pack, Product DoD, replay, ledger, and VSIX behavior.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new artifact is a release-readiness assessment and guard, not a runtime RPC, diagnostic endpoint, report wrapper, dashboard, or user-facing summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Observable Runtime protocol behavior is preserved; the implementation change moves task.list transport-bound helpers into task_progress and adds guard pressure that fails future module-boundary drift before release.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless controllers can rely on bounded Runtime authority modules and checked source metrics rather than an unresolved monolith-risk claim.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the P1 runtime-module-decomposition-reevaluation blocker while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until runtime-release-guard-ci, platform/deadline/durability hardening, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: docs/architecture/runtime-module-decomposition-assessment.json records exact Runtime source metrics, lib.rs production/test split, authority hotspot counts, extracted module boundaries, non-authority rules, remaining risks, and closure rationale.

handle_task_list and task-list transport-bound helpers move from crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs to crates/brownie-runtime/src/task_progress.rs, colocating task.list output bounding with task progress overview projection.

scripts/guard-runtime-module-decomposition.mjs validates the assessment against live source metrics, required boundary tokens, lib.rs ceilings, task_progress ownership, and non-authority rules; its tests cover drift back into lib.rs, missing task_progress ownership, and metric tampering.
The phase does not set runtime_release_ready=true, change license/publish/release metadata, or start CI/platform hardening; remaining P0/P1 blockers stay open.

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or changes license/publish/release metadata
module extraction changes JSON-RPC, ledger, replay, permission, MCP, Mode Pack, Product DoD, Product Completion, or VSIX behavior
task.list transport bounds move back into lib.rs or away from task_progress without updating guarded evidence
the assessment metrics, boundary tokens, or lib.rs production/test ceilings drift without guard failure

CLI, VSIX, external controller state, prose, model output, raw prompts, provider output, file contents, paths, secrets, environment values, executable content, or process output are treated as Runtime authority or decomposition evidence

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-6 changes guard-engine files, the current phase manifest, and Runtime release-readiness audit while closing runtime-module-decomposition-reevaluation. Review must confirm the task.list move is behavior-preserving, assessment metrics match source, guard negative tests fail closed, Runtime authority remains in Rust, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: Runtime module decomposition assessment records file line counts, public/private item counts, state mutation, durable write, permission, recovery, RPC dispatch, approval, MCP, Product DoD, diagnostics, dependency-boundary, and test-corpus evidence.
task.list handler and transport-bound helpers are owned by task_progress rather than lib.rs.
guard:runtime-module-decomposition fails on metric drift, missing boundary tokens, or task.list ownership regression.
The existing VSIX check path invokes guard:runtime-module-decomposition, and the release-readiness guard requires that invocation.
Runtime Release Ready remains false and remaining non-RRP-6 blockers stay open.
behavior_evidence: cargo check -p brownie-runtime verifies the task.list extraction compiles with existing Runtime types and call sites.
pnpm guard:runtime-module-decomposition validates the assessment against live source.
pnpm guard:runtime-module-decomposition:test covers negative module-boundary and metric drift cases.
pnpm check runs the new guard through the existing VSIX check path.

accepted_capability: Runtime module decomposition reevaluation now has an executable assessment and guard.
task.list transport-bound ownership is physically moved into task_progress.
Future module-boundary drift fails before release.
behavior_evidence: cargo check -p brownie-runtime validates the behavior-preserving Rust move.
pnpm guard:runtime-module-decomposition validates the repository assessment.
pnpm guard:runtime-module-decomposition:test exercises negative drift cases.
pnpm check invokes the new guard through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, MCP, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as decomposition evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not start CI workflow hardening, platform/deadline/durability hardening, hosted scheduler/daemon/adapter work, or broad runtime redesign.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected continuing unbounded M64.x extraction because RRP-6 is a finite closure assessment, not a code-diet campaign.
Rejected moving RPC dispatch or generated proposal diagnostics in this phase because the assessment found higher churn than release-risk reduction.
Rejected docs-only closure because the debt needs executable drift detection and at least one concrete ownership cleanup.
technical_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci and platform-deadline-durability-hardening remain open Runtime blockers.
Owner license/publish/release decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue with platform/deadline/durability hardening or CI release-gate hardening as a separate bounded Runtime-owned phase.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-6 closes the local Runtime module-decomposition reevaluation blocker with a guarded assessment and bounded task.list extraction.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until remaining Runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing Runtime JSON-RPC and ledger semantics are preserved.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-6.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-6.
